module_microarchitecture.name: motor_control_top
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Single-clock top-level ASIC controller that instantiates and wires the register file, request packer, response unpacker, freshness/timeout monitor, command shaper, fault manager, and transaction controller using only synchronous control/state signals.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Use the transaction controller as the launch/accept gate, the freshness monitor as the safety gate, and the fault manager as the latched policy gate; propagate register-programmed limits and sequence state to the subordinate blocks and suppress model-derived activity whenever enable, freshness, or fault conditions disallow it.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Keep only small control/state registers and handshake flags at the top boundary; all state updates occur on clk with rst_n driving deterministic safe reset values, with no asynchronous data paths or bulk payload storage.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive the 32-bit register window response, the bounded 128-bit request stream, the bounded 128-bit response-ready handshake, and the 32-bit actuator command plus command_valid through the subordinate block owners, defaulting to safe fallback behavior when the safety chain is not satisfied.
ownership_notes: Must retain request/response, safety, timeout, and actuator-command behavior.
Does not expose geometry arrays, flow fields, surface-pressure grids, tensor inference outputs, or bulk payload memories.

module_microarchitecture.name: control_status_regfile
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Small synchronous 32-bit register file with explicit decode of the documented offsets and simple status mirroring logic; no inferred memories or payload arrays.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Accept bounded reg_write/reg_read transactions, update writable configuration fields only, and synchronize fault/sequence/status inputs into the readable status window.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Store only the documented configuration and status flops: control_enable, timeout cycles, clamp bounds, safe fallback command, expected_seq, model_ready, fault latch visibility, last_seq_seen, and last_error_code; clear all deterministically on reset.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Return reg_rdata and reg_ready synchronously and provide the semantic control/status outputs to the controller blocks without exporting any model payloads.
ownership_notes: Owns reg_rdata, reg_ready, control_enable, stream_timeout_cycles, min_actuator_cmd, max_actuator_cmd, safe_fallback_cmd, expected_seq, model_ready, last_seq_seen, last_error_code, and fault_clear.
Register access remains bounded to the defined 32-bit window.

module_microarchitecture.name: request_packer
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Compact packet builder that assembles a fixed 128-bit request format from control and sequencing inputs plus a descriptor handle and velocity field.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Assert req_valid only when control_enable, launch authorization, envelope validity, and req_ready handshake conditions permit a launch; otherwise hold a safe default and suppress packet issuance.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Use minimal registered packet/valid holding state only as needed to complete the handshake; no geometry expansion or large buffering is implied.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive req_packet with a deterministic packing order containing protocol version, command type, sequence number, geometry descriptor handle/identifier, stream_velocity_mps-related content, and a small integrity check, and assert packet_valid only for a fully formed launch candidate.
ownership_notes: Geometry is referenced only by handle/identifier, not expanded from STL.

module_microarchitecture.name: response_unpacker
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Compact 128-bit response decoder and validator that extracts only response status, response sequence, integrity outcome, and a command-relevant summary field.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Accept responses only when resp_valid and resp_ready permit a handshake and the packet passes header, integrity, freshness, and sequence checks; reject stale, malformed, or mismatched packets.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain only small decode/status registers needed for validation and summary extraction; no model-field expansion, CFD arrays, or tensor-like storage is introduced.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Emit resp_accepted, resp_stale, resp_malformed, resp_seq_mismatch, resp_integrity_ok, response_status, response_seq, and a 32-bit command_intent only when validation succeeds.
ownership_notes: Owns resp_accepted, resp_stale, resp_malformed, resp_seq_mismatch, resp_integrity_ok, response_status, response_seq, and command_intent.
No raw drag-force, lift-force, surface-pressure, or flow-field content is expanded internally.

module_microarchitecture.name: freshness_timeout_monitor
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Synchronous freshness and timeout supervisor for a single outstanding transaction, using a monotonic sequence check and a programmable cycle counter.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Track launch and response completion against stream_timeout_cycles and expected_seq, assert fault_set on stale/late/malformed/sequence-mismatch conditions, and request safe fallback whenever the transaction is not safe to continue.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Use one timeout counter, one outstanding-transaction indicator, and minimal sequence-tracking state; do not implement queues or broad buffering.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive safe_fallback_active, timeout_active, fault_set, seq_update_valid, and seq_update_value for downstream fault handling and register updates.
ownership_notes: Owns safe_fallback_active, timeout_active, fault_set, seq_update_valid, and seq_update_value.
Only one bounded outstanding transaction is tracked.

module_microarchitecture.name: command_shaper
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Final 32-bit command generator that clamps model-derived intent to configured min/max bounds and substitutes the safe fallback command whenever intent is invalid or unsafe.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Select between clamped intent, retained last-safe command if explicitly allowed and still in bounds, or safe_fallback_cmd based on intent_valid, safe_fallback_active, and fault_latched status.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Retain only a last-safe command register if policy permits; otherwise the output is purely combinational/registered from the current safe selection and reset-safe default.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive actuator_cmd and actuator_cmd_valid for the external interface and assert clamp_event when the intent is outside bounds and clamping is applied.
ownership_notes: The externally visible command remains 32 bits wide.

module_microarchitecture.name: fault_manager
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Latched fault aggregation block that collects fault causes, prioritizes a compact fault code, and holds the system in safe-fallback policy until software clears the latch.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Set fault_latched on fault_set_in and/or policy-triggering events, clear only on fault_clear, and deassert model-derived permission whenever control is disabled or a fault is present.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Store a single latched fault bit, compact fault code, and policy outputs with deterministic reset behavior; no additional history or payload storage is introduced.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive fault_latched, fault_code, safe_fallback_active, and model_ready as the authoritative policy/status outputs into the rest of the design and register file.
ownership_notes: Owns fault_latched, fault_code, safe_fallback_active, and model_ready.
Faults remain latched until software clears them.

module_microarchitecture.name: transaction_controller
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Small bounded transaction sequencer and handshake authority for one request-response in flight.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Authorize launch only when control_enable, safety gating, and fault policy permit; assert resp_ready only when a request is outstanding and response acceptance is allowed.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain one outstanding-transaction flag and minimal gating state with deterministic reset to idle; no large queues or multi-transaction machinery is implied.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive launch_req, request_active, resp_ready, request_permitted, and response_permitted to coordinate the request packer, response unpacker, freshness monitor, and command shaper.
ownership_notes: Owns launch_req, request_active, resp_ready, request_permitted, and response_permitted.
Enforces single-outstanding-transaction policy unless a small bounded counter is explicitly chosen.

fsm_intent.description: No complex FSM is implied beyond simple synchronous control/status, single-outstanding transaction bookkeeping, and safety gating; legal default transitions and reset-to-idle behavior are sufficient.

internal_storage: Small control/status flops, handshake flags, timeout/sequence state, fault latch, and output registers only
Writable control fields, readable status fields, last_seq_seen, last_error_code, and fault-clear pulse state
Optional registered packet hold and valid bit for handshake completion
Small decode registers for header/status/sequence/integrity checks
Outstanding-transaction flag, timeout counter, and sequence-tracking state
Latched fault bit and compact fault code
One outstanding-request flag and minimal gating state

sequencing_notes: Software programs the register file first, establishing enable, timeout, clamp bounds, safe fallback, and expected sequence values.
The transaction controller only authorizes a launch when the safety chain permits operation and the request packer can complete a bounded handshake.
Request launch is single-shot and bounded; only one outstanding transaction is tracked at a time.
The response unpacker validates the compact packet before any command intent is released to the command shaper.
The freshness monitor rejects stale, late, malformed, or sequence-mismatched responses and triggers fault handling.
The fault manager latches causes until software clears them through the register window.
timing_notes: All state is synchronous to clk with active-low rst_n providing deterministic reset.
No asynchronous data paths are required.
Handshake signals are sampled on the clock edge and held/advanced using simple registered control.
Combinational depth should remain modest by keeping decode, packing, validation, and clamping logic compact and localized.
Streaming buses remain at or below 128 bits, and the actuator command remains 32 bits with a separate validity strobe.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
